findings.claim: \(g\) is gravitational field strength (10 N/kg on Earth) - repeated by the flashcard answer '10 N/kg (approximately).'
findings.truth: The board's own figure for free-fall acceleration near Earth is about 9.8 m/s2, and the spec says the value of g will be given in any calculation. Lesson 10 of this same unit already uses 9.8 N/kg, so the unit contradicts itself. Article now states about 9.8 N/kg and says the worked examples round to 10.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.1.2 'In any calculation the value of the gravitational field strength (g) will be given'; spec 6.5.4.2.2 'an acceleration of about 9.8 m/s2'

findings.claim: If a question says 'calculate,' you must use an equation - you will not get marks for just stating the answer.
findings.truth: A correct final answer scores the answer mark on its own. Working is worth showing because it earns method marks when the answer is wrong, not because a bare answer scores nothing.
findings.evidence: settled exam practice; the spec's assessment section sets no such rule

findings.claim: The whole 'Reducing Unwanted Energy Transfers' section (thermal insulation, lubrication, wall thickness and thermal conductivity) sits inside a higher-only wrapper, so Foundation students never see it.
findings.truth: None of that is Higher tier. Only 'describe ways to increase the efficiency of an intended energy transfer' carries the HT flag, and that is a separate key-fact box which is gated correctly. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.2.1 (no HT marker) vs spec 6.1.2.2 '(HT only) Students should be able to describe ways to increase the efficiency'

findings.claim: Flashcard 'Name one way to increase the efficiency of a mechanical device.' is untagged, while the article gates the same material as Higher.
findings.truth: That statement is HT only, so the flashcard now carries a '(Higher tier)' prefix.
findings.evidence: spec 6.1.2.2 (HT only)

findings.claim: Ohm's Law states that V = I x R ... This relationship only applies to ohmic conductors at constant temperature.
findings.truth: V = IR is the definition of resistance and is used for every component, including filament lamps and diodes; a student who thinks it cannot be applied to a lamp will refuse a calculation that is worth marks. What is limited to ohmic conductors at constant temperature is the proportionality, i.e. R staying constant.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.1.3 'Current, potential difference or resistance can be calculated using the equation V = IR' (no restriction); spec 6.2.1.4 restricts only the direct proportionality

findings.claim: The reciprocal formula 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 (+ 1/R3) is taught in L3 and L4 as Higher-tier content, and L4's conclusion drills it as a key takeaway to all tiers.
findings.truth: It is not Higher-tier content, it is outside the specification for this qualification altogether. Both places now say the course does not ask for this calculation, and the L4 takeaway states the examinable rule instead (total resistance is less than the smallest resistor).
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.2 'Students are not required to calculate the total resistance of two resistors joined in parallel.'

findings.claim: a frequency of 50 Hz. This means the current changes direction 50 times per second.
findings.truth: 50 Hz means 50 complete cycles per second. Each cycle reverses the current twice, so the current changes direction 100 times per second. This is a named misconception and the sentence taught it as fact.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.3.1 (50 Hz supply); definition of frequency as cycles per second

findings.claim: Tooltip and glossary define a circuit breaker as 'An automatic switch that breaks a circuit when it detects a difference between the live and neutral currents.'
findings.truth: That describes a residual current device. The circuit breaker the lesson text describes (does the fuse's job, can be reset) trips on excess current. The tooltip contradicted the sentence it was attached to.
findings.evidence: settled fact; the lesson's own key-fact text 'does the same job but can be reset instead of replaced'

findings.claim: The whole National Grid explanation (high voltage, low current, step-up and step-down transformers) sits inside a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: Only the transformer equation Vp Ip = Vs Is is HT only in this spec, and the lesson does not give it. Explaining why the grid is efficient is required of all students, and the lesson's own knowledge check and practice question already ask Foundation students about it. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.4.3: main content unmarked, 'Higher tier only' applies solely to the transformer equation

findings.claim: Glossary tooltip on 'mass': 'The amount of substance in a given volume.'
findings.truth: That is a definition of density, in a lesson whose whole point is to separate mass from density. Mass is the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms.
findings.evidence: spec 6.3.1.1 (density = mass/volume); settled fact

findings.claim: The 'Particle Model Explanation' section (particle behaviour during melting, boiling, condensing and freezing) sits inside a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: Nothing in the particle model topic is Higher tier in this specification, and this is core Foundation material that the lesson's own practice questions ask about. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.3.1 to 6.3.3: no (HT only) marker anywhere in the topic

findings.claim: Practice question 5 is labelled '9 marks - Evaluate' with a 7-9 / 4-6 / 1-3 band ladder.
findings.truth: There is no 9-mark question in this qualification. Every paper is 70 marks over 1 hour 15 minutes with multiple choice, structured, closed short answer and open response; extended response tops out at 6 marks. Retagged as 6 marks with a rescaled ladder.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Physics Paper 1)

findings.claim: Practice question 6 is labelled '12 marks - Extended Response'.
findings.truth: Same as F12: no 12-mark question exists on this paper. Retagged as 6 marks; the answer content was already a 6-mark method list.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Physics Paper 1)

findings.claim: The alpha, beta and gamma properties box (penetration, range, ionising power, effect on mass and atomic number) sits inside a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: Those properties are the required knowledge for all students, and the lesson's own knowledge checks, flashcards and practice questions test them untiered. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4.2.1 'Required knowledge of the properties of alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays is limited to their penetration through materials, their range in air and ionising power' (no HT marker)

findings.claim: The contamination and irradiation box sits inside a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: Radioactive contamination is untiered content and the lesson's own 4-mark practice question asks all students to compare the two hazards. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4.2.4 Radioactive contamination (no HT marker)

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches static electricity, charging by friction, sparking, earthing, electric fields, field lines and uses of static as examined content.
findings.truth: None of it is in this specification. The Electricity topic runs 6.2.1 to 6.2.4 and stops at the National Grid; there is no static electricity or electric field statement anywhere in the physics content, and 'electrostatic' appears only as an example of a non-contact force in Forces, which is on the other physics paper. The physics is accurate, so the content is kept and now carries a 'Separate Physics only' label at the top of the article and in the description.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2 (6.2.1-6.2.4 only); grep of the whole spec finds no 'static electricity', no 'electric field', no Van de Graaff

findings.claim: Question 1 is worth 1 mark but its scheme awards two marking points; question 2 is worth 2 marks but its scheme awards three.
findings.truth: A scheme that credits more points than the question is worth teaches students to write too much for the marks on offer. Both schemes trimmed to the stated marks.
findings.evidence: internal consistency of the question type and its scheme

findings.claim: The lesson teaches Boyle's law (p1V1 = p2V2), pressure in fluids (p = h rho g), atmospheric pressure, upthrust and hydraulic systems as examined content.
findings.truth: Only the opening section is in scope. This specification's whole treatment of pressure is qualitative: molecules in constant random motion, temperature linked to average kinetic energy, and pressure changing with temperature at constant volume. There is no pressure equation, no pressure-volume relationship, no fluid or atmospheric pressure and no upthrust anywhere in the physics content; in the separate qualification most of that also sits on the other physics paper. The physics is accurate (all four calculations recompute correctly), so the content is kept and a scope note now names the out-of-scope sections.
findings.evidence: spec 6.3.3.1 Particle motion in gases is the only pressure content; grep of the whole spec finds no 'atmospheric pressure', 'pressure in fluids', 'upthrust' or work done on a gas

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches nuclear fission, chain reactions, reactor components, nuclear fusion, E = mc2, binding energy per nucleon, medical and industrial uses of radiation and nuclear waste categories as examined content.
findings.truth: None of it is in this specification. The Atomic structure topic runs 6.4.1 to 6.4.2.4 and ends at radioactive contamination; the words fission, fusion and background radiation do not appear in the physics content at all, and binding energy per nucleon is post-16 material. The physics is accurate (the mass-defect calculation recomputes to 3.56 x 10^-28 kg), so the content is kept and now carries a 'Separate Physics only' label at the top of the article and in the description.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4 (6.4.1-6.4.2.4 only); grep of the whole spec finds no nuclear fission, no nuclear fusion, no background radiation, no medical tracer

findings.claim: Lesson 9 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both' in a Physics Paper 1 unit.
findings.truth: A label is the safe interim fix, but the lesson's place in the unit is Tom's call. Options: (a) keep it as a labelled extension lesson, which is what the edits assume; (b) move it into the separate-sciences board where it is examined and drop it from this unit; (c) retire it. Recommendation: (a) now, (b) at the next rebuild, because a Combined student who revises this lesson spends a whole lesson's effort on nothing that can be examined.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2 scope; see F16

findings.claim: Roughly 85% of lesson 10 (everything after the opening particle-model section) is outside this qualification.
findings.truth: The in-scope part is one section long, which is too thin to carry a lesson on its own. Options: (a) keep the labelled lesson as built; (b) rewrite it as a short in-scope lesson on particle motion and gas pressure and move the fluid-pressure material to the separate-sciences board. Recommendation: (b) at the next rebuild; the label holds until then.
findings.evidence: spec 6.3.3.1; see F18

findings.claim: Lesson 11 is wholly outside this qualification and is published live at tier 'both'.
findings.truth: Same choice as F20. Recommendation: keep the labelled lesson now, move it to the separate-sciences board at the next rebuild.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4 scope; see F19

findings.claim: Three lessons of this eleven-lesson unit teach out-of-scope material while several required statements of the four in-scope topics are not taught anywhere in the unit.
findings.truth: Missing: nuclear equations for alpha and beta decay, which the spec requires students to balance (6.4.2.2); mass number, atomic number and isotopes (6.4.1.2); atomic radius about 1 x 10^-10 m and the nucleus less than 1/10000 of that (6.4.1.1). Three of the four required practicals for this paper are also never named as required practicals: specific heat capacity (L7 describes the method inside a practice question only), resistance of a wire and combinations of resistors (L3 does not mention it), and density of regular solids, irregular solids and liquids by displacement (L6 does not mention it). Only the I-V characteristics practical is labelled, in L4. Filling these gaps means authoring new sections and re-narrating, which is beyond a surgical edit.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4.1.1, 6.4.1.2, 6.4.2.2; required practical activities 14, 15 and 17

findings.claim: A Higher-tier collapsible gives P = Fv and a flashcard drills it.
findings.truth: P = Fv is correct physics but is on neither the recall list nor the equation sheet for this qualification, so it is extension rather than Higher-tier content. Left as it is: it is boxed, it is true, and relabelling it would ripple through narration for no mark gain.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B: neither the recall list nor the equation sheet contains P = Fv

findings.claim: 'By combining this with Ohm's law, we get two more useful equations: P = I^2 R and P = V^2 / R.'
findings.truth: P = I2R is on the recall list; P = V2/R is not on either list for this qualification. It is correct physics and derivable, so it is left as extension.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B equations 17 and 18

findings.claim: L8 lists uses of radiation (medical tracers, sterilising equipment, thickness gauges, smoke detectors), which the separate qualification covers in its own section.
findings.truth: This is allowed here. The spec asks students to 'apply their knowledge to the uses of radiation and evaluate the best sources of radiation to use in a given situation', which is exactly what the sentence and the smoke-detector practice question do. No edit. The same material in L11 is different: there it is taught as a topic in its own right alongside fission and fusion.
findings.evidence: spec 6.4.2.1 final statement

findings.claim: L2 description is 103 characters.
findings.truth: The house validator limit is under 100 characters, so this row may block a later validation run. Not a factual error, so not edited here. L4's is exactly 100.
findings.evidence: house validator limit

summary: Eleven lessons checked; 27 findings (9 HIGH, 12 MEDIUM, 6 LOW; 19 FIX, 4 ADJUDICATE, 4 NOTE) and 33 edits. Every calculation in the unit recomputes correctly and the radioactivity, atomic-model and circuit facts are sound, so the yield is not random error: it is two systemic build faults. First, lessons 9, 10 and 11 teach separate-science material (static electricity and electric fields; Boyle's law, fluid and atmospheric pressure, upthrust, hydraulics; fission, fusion and nuclear waste) as if examined, which is roughly a quarter of the unit; the content is accurate so it is kept and labelled, with the placement decision left to Tom. Second, the higher-only wrapper was applied to five sections that are not Higher tier at all (insulation and lubrication, the National Grid, the particle model of state changes, the alpha/beta/gamma properties, contamination and irradiation), hiding required Foundation content that the same lessons then test untiered. The only outright factual errors are the 50 Hz claim in L5, the RCD definition given for a circuit breaker in L5, the density definition given for mass in L6, the claim that V = IR only works for ohmic conductors in L3, and two invented 9-mark and 12-mark question formats in L7.
